headlines.title: 홈플러스 근로자 생계비 410억원 지원 … 협력업체 금융지원 5.2조

headlines.title: [단독] 월세 가격까지 치솟자…정부, 월세 세액공제 혜택 늘린다

key_headlines.title: Trump Administration Imposes Forced Labor Tariffs on 60 Countries Including South Korea at 12.5%
key_headlines.summary: The Trump administration has imposed forced labor tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act on 60 trading partners, with South Korea facing a 12.5% tariff rate. The tariffs took effect on July 24, 2026.

key_headlines.title: South Korea Designated as Currency Surveillance Country for Fourth Consecutive Time by US
key_headlines.summary: The US Treasury has retained South Korea on its currency surveillance list for the fourth consecutive time, though acknowledging the won's weakness does not match Korea's strong economic fundamentals. The won has fallen to around 1,460 per dollar.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Average Jeonse Price Exceeds 700 Million Won Amid Monthly Rental Crisis
key_headlines.summary: Seoul's average apartment jeonse (long-term lease) price has surpassed 700 million won for the first time since 2021, with some units in Gangdong-gu reaching 920 million won. The shortage of jeonse inventory has driven prices up sharply over the past year.

key_headlines.title: Government to Expand Monthly Rent Tax Deduction Benefits to Ease Housing Burden
key_headlines.summary: The government plans to expand monthly rent tax deduction benefits in tax reform amendments to be announced in early August to help reduce housing expenses for renters. This comes as monthly rent prices continue to rise across the country.

key_headlines.title: International Oil Prices Surge Amid Red Sea Crisis, Threatening Second-Half Inflation Goals
key_headlines.summary: Brent crude prices have surged to over 100 dollars per barrel following attacks by Houthi militants on tankers in the Red Sea, threatening Korea's goal to maintain inflation below 3% for the second half of 2026. The Bank of Korea may accelerate rate hikes if inflation pressures persist.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Trump administration's imposition of 12.5% forced labor tariffs on South Korea and 59 other trading partners has escalated trade tensions, while domestic economic pressures mount from surging international oil prices triggered by Red Sea geopolitical instability. The government has activated emergency response measures including a four-week freeze on maximum fuel prices and emergency spending of 350 billion won on food supply stabilization. Housing affordability remains critical, with Seoul apartment jeonse prices exceeding 700 million won and monthly rents rising sharply, prompting the government to expand monthly rent tax deductions. The Bank of Korea's recent rate hike to 2.75% may be followed by another increase in August if inflation remains elevated, creating policy tensions as fiscal stimulus could conflict with monetary tightening.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% on July 16, with analysts predicting another increase in August if consumer inflation remains elevated following strong second-quarter economic growth. International oil price surges driven by Red Sea tensions present a significant upside risk to inflation, potentially forcing the central bank to accelerate rate increases and jeopardizing the second-half inflation target of 3%. The government is issuing 67 trillion won in public bonds in the third quarter, 4 trillion won more than initially planned due to rising policy demands, while managing fiscal risks amid monetary tightening. Tax reform amendments planned for early August will include expanded monthly rent tax deductions to address growing housing cost burdens for low-income renters.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI declined below 6,000 points amid semiconductor earnings uncertainty and geopolitical concerns, though analysts note the market could rebound if the US Federal Reserve holds rates steady at its July 28-29 FOMC meeting and foreign investors resume purchases. Bank demand deposits have declined significantly from their 2022 highs as investors shift funds toward higher-yielding fixed-term deposits, with approximately 41 trillion won in bank reserves available for potential equity market entry at cheaper valuations. Samsung Electronics' record second-quarter earnings of 171 trillion won in revenue and 89.4 trillion won in operating profit have set expectations high for SK Hynix and other semiconductor firms reporting this week. The upcoming FOMC decision and major tech earnings announcements from Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Apple are critical catalysts that will determine foreign investor sentiment and KOSPI's recovery potential toward 7,000.
sections.Industry & Technology: Domestic battery makers are posting improved second-quarter earnings driven by increased electric vehicle demand and expanded energy storage system orders, with expectations that the global high oil price environment will accelerate the end of EV demand stagnation earlier than anticipated. Samsung Electronics has implemented titanium-based display technology and silicon-carbon battery innovations in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, simultaneously improving screen wrinkles, durability, thickness, weight, and battery performance. The LS Group is expanding into AI-related materials and components including robotics, batteries, rare earth elements, and EV charging infrastructure, positioning itself to capitalize on a decade-long boom in power equipment demand. Korea's three major battery companies, along with Ecopro, Aekyung, and Solvrain, are partnering to establish a sodium-ion battery supply ecosystem featuring abundant raw materials, excellent price competitiveness, safety, longevity, and low-temperature performance.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's average apartment jeonse price has exceeded 700 million won for the first time since 2021, with some units reaching 920 million won, as revised housing lease protection laws continue to restrict supply and drive prices upward. Monthly rental prices are simultaneously rising across the country, creating a triple surge in apartment transactions, leases, and monthly rents that is severely burdening housing-cost-conscious consumers. The government is expanding monthly rent tax deduction benefits through tax reforms to provide relief to renters, while supply-constrained areas are offering long-term housing guarantees, though underlying affordability challenges persist. Officetels remain relatively stagnant despite rising apartment prices due to housing unit counting regulations that restrict supply, with industry experts suggesting regulatory relief could redirect real estate demand from apartments to alternative housing types.
sections.International Economy: The Trump administration's imposition of Section 301 forced labor tariffs on 60 trading partners, including South Korea's 12.5% rate, has escalated trade tensions and sparked criticism from Democratic opponents who characterize the move as a pretext rather than legitimate policy. The US Treasury has maintained South Korea on its currency surveillance list for a fourth consecutive time, though acknowledging Korean foreign exchange authorities have conducted net dollar sales to support the won and that recent weakness does not reflect Korea's strong economic fundamentals. The US Federal Reserve's July FOMC meeting outcome will be critical for global markets, with expectations of rate maintenance potentially stabilizing bond yields and exchange rates and supporting foreign investor flows into Korean equities. International oil prices have surged to over 100 dollars per barrel amid Red Sea geopolitical tensions, creating inflation pressures in the US and globally while major American technology firms including Microsoft, Meta, and Google oppose proposed open-source AI model regulations that could weaken US competitiveness against China.
sections.AI & Economy: Major global technology firms including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, and Google have publicly opposed proposed regulations on open-source AI models, arguing that restricting open-weight AI systems would undermine US leadership and competitive advantage against China rather than strengthen it. Domestic Korean IT firms have secured major AI infrastructure commitments including Naver's 10 billion dollar investment and SK Telecom's large-scale data center expansion alongside Nvidia and other global partners, establishing a combined 5 gigawatt capacity supporting approximately 2 million AI GPUs. SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and other major semiconductor and electronic component manufacturers are reporting record second-quarter earnings this week, benefiting from surging AI data center investments that have increased demand for high-bandwidth memory, server DRAM, and specialized components. Samsung Electronics' record 171 trillion won second-quarter revenue and 89.4 trillion won operating profit were driven by strong AI server memory demand, with SK Hynix expected to post record earnings and other electronics firms benefiting from AI infrastructure expansion.
sections.Others: Chip prices are surging as memory manufacturers gain leverage over downstream customers, with Micron's CEO dismissing arguments that Chinese alternatives could control inflation, while Trump administration officials face industry lobbying on tariff policy implications. The government is pursuing comprehensive outreach to US administration, Congress, and business communities to address potential Section 301 tariff escalations, with officials like Industry Minister Yeo Han-koo actively engaging US counterparts to prevent additional tariffs. The government plans to restructure fund evaluation systems beginning next year, exempting funds with clearly defined establishment purposes from existing evaluation requirements to reduce administrative burden on fund managers. Optical communications infrastructure companies focused on high-speed data transmission for AI systems are experiencing exceptional growth as the AI competitive frontier shifts from GPU hardware to data center networking capabilities.
